_about: Peer-reviewed research on the invasive species recorded in the parks. Every source is a journal article with a DOI, published in or after the policy year. Every row carries verbatim quotes from the paper's abstract. Rule: no paper, no row. scripts/verify_citations.py checks each paper against Crossref and OpenAlex and each quote against the abstract. The summaries restate what the papers report, with the setting of each study.

playbooks.summary: Field trials with rabbit-derived scent lures (feces, urine and hair) found no difference in python detections between lure plots (4) and soil controls (7). The authors conclude that mammalian scent lures alone are insufficient to attract pythons.
playbooks.region_note: 21 paired plots at three study sites in the Greater Everglades, June to September 2022.
quotes: We detected 11 pythons during our study, but there was no difference between controls with soil (n = 7) and treatments (n = 4).
Our experiment indicates that mammalian scent lures alone are insufficient to attract pythons.

playbooks.summary: Environmental DNA analysis of water samples detects shed DNA and gives high detection probabilities for a snake that is extremely cryptic. The authors used it to estimate python occupancy at wading bird colonies.
playbooks.region_note: Tree islands in the central Everglades.
quotes: we utilized environmental DNA (eDNA) analysis-a genetic tool which detects shed DNA in water samples and provides high detection probabilities
Burmese pythons (hereafter "pythons") are extremely cryptic and there has been no efficient way to detect them

playbooks.summary: A review of the science on managing Burmese pythons describes the existing control tools, reviews the challenges to research and identifies key knowledge gaps. It describes pythons as extremely challenging to detect because of inaccessible habitat and their cryptic nature.
playbooks.region_note: Greater Everglades Ecosystem, southern Florida. A review and synthesis.
quotes: We describe existing control tools and review challenges to productive research, identifying key knowledge gaps that would improve future research and decision making for python control.
rendering them extremely challenging to detect

playbooks.summary: In Kibale National Park, short-term management of Lantana by cutting and uprooting did not promote tree establishment, and the tree community in cleared areas was not converging on uninvaded forest. The authors conclude that sustained follow-up clearing of dense shrubs, herbs and resprouted Lantana is key to long-term recovery.
playbooks.region_note: Kibale National Park, Uganda; cleared, invaded and uninvaded plots compared.
quotes: The short-term management of Lantana did not promote tree establishment.
Sustained follow-up clearing of dense secondary shrubs and herbs and resprouted L. camara in cleared areas is key to ensuring long-term recovery of the forest tree community.

playbooks.summary: A review of the literature from India describes Lantana as tenacious in its resistance to cutting and burning and puts the cost of control at US$70 per hectare. It concludes that economic uses outweigh the negative impacts and that cost-benefit studies are needed before eradication.
playbooks.region_note: India. A review of studies reported from India.
quotes: tenacious resistance to cutting and burning
the cost of its control is estimated at US$ 70 per ha

playbooks.summary: A review reports that mechanical, chemical, biological and cultural controls are used against Senna spectabilis with varying degrees of success, and that eradication efforts include complete uprooting, girdling and debarking, followed by native vegetation reinstatement and soil restoration.
quotes: Various methods, including mechanical, chemical, biological, and cultural controls, are utilized to combat Senna spectabilis infestations, albeit with varying degrees of success.
Eradication endeavors encompass techniques like complete uprooting, girdling, and debarking

playbooks.summary: In two wildlife sanctuaries in Telangana the authors report that manual removal of the weed before flowering is the effective means to limit its spread, in comparison with the biological and chemical methods attempted.
playbooks.region_note: Kinnerasani and Eturnagaram wildlife sanctuaries, Telangana, India. A field report without a controlled comparison.
quotes: The manual removal of this weed (mechanical method) before flowering is the effective means to mitigate the spread of the species in comparison to the biological
and chemical (Glyphosate, Triclopyrester) methods attempted

playbooks.summary: In a two-year field experiment, a pre-emergent herbicide dramatically reduced Microstegium vimineum in the second year but not most resident plants, which were perennials and indirectly benefited at a more productive site.
playbooks.region_note: A two-year field experiment in natural plant communities; the abstract does not name the site.
quotes: The pre-emergent herbicide dramatically reduced M. vimineum in year 2 of the study, but not most resident plants

playbooks.summary: In oak woodlands in the eastern United States, a single application of a pre-emergent herbicide significantly reduced Microstegium vimineum density, and the invader had not fully recovered at either site by 2025. The herbicide had immediate but short-lived negative effects on some native species recruiting from seed at the less productive site.
playbooks.region_note: Oak woodlands in the eastern United States; two sites, measured in 2019, 2024 and 2025.
quotes: The herbicide significantly reduced M. vimineum density in 2019.
The herbicide had immediate but short-lived negative effects on some native species recruiting from seed at the less productive site.

playbooks.summary: A benefit-risk analysis reports that releases of lady beetles and derodontid beetles have provided limited control of the hemlock woolly adelgid. It finds that biological control agents have not yet produced a net ecological benefit at current suppression levels, though stacking several agents could.
playbooks.region_note: Eastern North America. An analysis of introduced biological control agents.
quotes: have provided limited control of HWA
BCAs have not as yet resulted in a net ecological benefit under current suppression levels, but stacking multiple BCAs could lead to a positive BRI under estimated suppression levels

playbooks.summary: A study of imidacloprid applied to the bark and to the soil, at high and low rates, found basal bark treatments as effective as soil treatments and concluded that bark treatment can be an effective method for controlling the hemlock woolly adelgid.
playbooks.region_note: Eastern hemlock trees; the abstract does not name the site.
quotes: The results showed that basal bark treatments were as effective as soil treatments.
Hence, basal bark treatments of imidacloprid can be an effective method for control of HWAs in eastern hemlock trees.

playbooks.summary: In Nova Scotia hemlock stands, imidacloprid treatment increased eastern red-backed salamander abundance compared with untreated infested stands. The authors read this as support for integrating chemical control with long-term monitoring while biological control develops.
playbooks.region_note: Hemlock stands in southwestern Nova Scotia, Canada; treated, untreated and uninfested stands compared.
quotes: Treatment and infestation were the only predictors of abundance: treatment increased abundance, whereas infestation reduced it.
These results reinforce the value of integrating chemical control with long-term monitoring while biological control strategies develop.

playbooks.summary: In the Banni grasslands, mechanical removal of Prosopis juliflora gave threefold higher native herb richness and sixfold higher cover than the control over four years, while lopping did not differ significantly from the control. Neither treatment restored the perennial grasses of the reference grasslands, removal is costly at larger scales, and the authors describe its removal as involving complex trade-offs.
playbooks.region_note: Banni grasslands, India; eight sites, randomised block design, four years.
quotes: We found native herbaceous plant richness and cover to be threefold (mean = 6 species) and sixfold (mean = 18% cover) higher, respectively, in the mechanical-removal treatment compared to the control
mechanically removing Prosopis is costly, especially at larger scales
its removal involves complex trade-offs

playbooks.summary: In Australian grasslands, a mixture of mostly native pasture species suppressed parthenium weed re-establishment by 78% compared with the control, and a mixture of mostly introduced species could not suppress it.
playbooks.region_note: Australian grasslands; planted mixtures compared with a control.
quotes: This mixture suppressed parthenium weed re-establishment by 78% compared to the control treatment.
However, the mixture was unable to suppress the growth of parthenium weed.

playbooks.summary: Experimental stream results suggest that removing introduced brown trout may help native brook trout expand and persist in downstream reaches, depending in part on where groundwater upwelling zones lie.
playbooks.region_note: Experimental streams; brook trout are native to eastern North America.
quotes: Our results indicate that removal of introduced brown trout may facilitate native brook trout expansion and population viability in downstream reaches depending in part on the spatial configuration of groundwater upwelling zones.

playbooks.summary: Over 13 years that included two wildfires, recruitment of Melaleuca after the second fire was 96.5% smaller than after the first, and biological control agents slowed seedling growth. The authors advise managers to prioritise removing large reproductive trees over treating recently recruited populations.
playbooks.region_note: A seasonally inundated wetland; the abstract does not name the site.
quotes: there was a downward trend in their overall invasiveness at this site, with progressively smaller recruitment cohorts due to biological control agents
Land managers should prioritize removing large reproductive trees over treating recently recruited populations

playbooks.summary: No-choice tests on 68 plant species found the moth Callopistria exotica highly specific to Old World climbing fern and one other exotic invasive fern, and climate modelling found very high suitability in south Florida. The authors expect its release to assist management of the fern.
playbooks.region_note: Quarantine tests of a moth collected in Hong Kong, with climate modelling for Florida.
quotes: The results indicated that C. exotica is highly specific to the target weed, L. microphyllum and a congener that is also an exotic invasive, L. japonicum.
The release of C. exotica is expected to assist in the effort to manage the invasive weed Old World climbing fern.

playbooks.summary: Revised rearing protocols for the biological control mite Floracarus perrepae raised gall abundance by 165.3% and mites per plant by 453.2%. The authors report that the larger releases improved establishment, abundance and impact of the agent across the invaded range in Florida.
playbooks.region_note: Mass rearing and releases as part of the Comprehensive Everglades Restoration Plan, Florida.
quotes: These changes have resulted in substantial improvements in gall abundance (165.3%), F. perrepae density per gall (86.0%), and estimated F. perrepae per plant (453.2%).
low establishment rates observed from 2008 to 2010

playbooks.summary: A review reports that the biological control agents released in Hawaii have had minimal impact and that the weed continues to be a difficult problem. Tests of two newer agents, a thrips and a foliage-gall former, indicate that they will safely contribute to control.
playbooks.region_note: Southeastern United States and Hawaii. A review of the biological control project.
quotes: However, the control agents have had minimal impact, and the weed continues to be a difficult problem.
Results of no-choice and choice trials conducted overseas and in quarantine indicate that both species will safely contribute to the control of this invasive weed.

impact_findings.affected: nest predation on turtle nests, and the mammals that prey on the nests
impact_findings.summary: Artificial turtle nests were rarely preyed on in the southern Everglades, where pythons have been established longest and few mammals were found, and very often preyed on at sites with few or no pythons. The author reports the first documentation of potential indirect effects of pythons on non-prey species and suggests that the loss of mammals is producing trophic cascades.
impact_findings.region_note: Artificial turtle nests (N = 183) at 13 sites across the expanding range of the python population in southern Florida.
quotes: I documented few mammals and low rates of nest predation (average score = 1.5 on a 1–5 scale) in the southern Everglades where pythons have been established the longest
and very high (average score = 4.6) rates of nest predation at sites with few or no pythons
suggest that loss or decline of mammals is resulting in trophic cascades that threaten the Everglades ecosystem

impact_findings.affected: large mammals, and the mosquito hosts that depend on them
impact_findings.summary: Mosquito blood meals taken from the hispid cotton rat, the main reservoir host of Everglades virus, rose from 14.7% in 1979 to 76.8% in 2016, while blood meals from deer, raccoons and opossums fell by 98.2%. The authors attribute the decline of these larger mammals to python predation and predict a higher risk of exposure to the virus, which they did not test.
impact_findings.region_note: Florida Everglades; mosquito blood meals compared between 1979 and 2016.
quotes: while blood meals from deer, raccoons and opossums decreased by 98.2%, reflecting precipitous declines in relative abundance of these larger mammals, attributed to python predation
although this was not tested in the current study

impact_findings.summary: Environmental DNA sampling found python DNA on tree islands holding wading bird colonies at a higher rate (occupancy 0.88) than on control islands with no breeding birds (0.42) between April and June. The authors suggest pythons are attracted to colonies and say monitoring is needed to determine the effect on bird populations.
impact_findings.region_note: Tree islands in the central Everglades, April to June; 15 colony and control pairs.
quotes: site-level python eDNA occupancy rates were higher at wading bird colonies
Continued monitoring of wading bird colonies is warranted to determine the effect pythons are having on populations

impact_findings.summary: A review of the science on managing Burmese pythons reports that pythons have severely impacted native species and ecosystems in Florida and calls them one of the most intractable invasive-species management issues in the world.
impact_findings.region_note: Greater Everglades Ecosystem, southern Florida. A review and synthesis.
quotes: Pythons have severely impacted native species and ecosystems in Florida and represent one of the most intractable invasive-species management issues across the globe.

impact_findings.affected: forests, pasture land, biodiversity and ecosystem services in India
impact_findings.summary: A review of the literature from India reports that Lantana has invaded vast tracts of dry and moist forest and other wasteland, has invaded most Indian pasture land (13.2 million ha) and has potentially altered biodiversity, landscape ecology and ecosystem services. The review also concludes that its positive impacts and economic uses outweigh its negative impacts and asks for cost-benefit studies before eradication decisions.
impact_findings.region_note: India. A review of studies reported from India.
quotes: Lantana has invaded vast tracts of dry-moist forests and other culturable wastelands, and has potentially altered biodiversity, landscape ecology and ecosystem services
the positive impacts and economic uses of Lantana outweigh its negative impacts and require further studies on cost-benefit considerations for decision making for its eradication and management

impact_findings.affected: tree species richness and ecosystem carbon
impact_findings.summary: In tropical dry deciduous forest in Madhya Pradesh, invaded sites had significantly lower tree species richness, juvenile tree carbon, total tree carbon and total biomass carbon than uninvaded sites, and richness fell as Lantana density rose. Shrub, litter and soil organic carbon were higher in invaded sites.
impact_findings.region_note: Tropical dry deciduous forests of Madhya Pradesh, India; invaded and uninvaded sites compared.
quotes: Significantly lower species richness (SR), C storage of juveniles, total trees, and total biomass C were observed in LI sites than in UI sites.
A significant negative relationship was observed between L. camara density and SR

impact_findings.affected: forest regeneration, and tree, shrub and herb cover
impact_findings.summary: In Kibale National Park, plots invaded by Lantana had lower tree, shrub and herb cover and diversity, and tree regeneration was suppressed.
impact_findings.region_note: Kibale National Park, Uganda (an African rainforest); invaded, cleared and uninvaded plots compared.
quotes: Lantana reduced tree, shrub, and herb cover and diversity, and suppressed tree regeneration.

impact_findings.summary: Senna spectabilis is commonly found in Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary. The study reports that it grows aggressively and can quickly cover open and degraded land, and that its reproductive strategy helps it colonise degraded areas and invade forest.
impact_findings.region_note: Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary, Kerala, India. Not one of the monitored parks.
quotes: Its aggressive growth rate and ability to quickly cover up open and degraded lands in forest ecosystems make it challenging to control its spread.
This reproductive strategy helps the taxon to colonise degraded areas and invade the forest ecosystem.

impact_findings.summary: A review of Senna spectabilis in India reports that its invasion results in habitat alteration, displacement of local flora and fauna and changes in trophic interactions, and that rapid growth, abundant seed production and allelopathic characteristics let it outcompete indigenous species.
impact_findings.region_note: India. A literature review.
quotes: Senna spectabilis invasion results in habitat alteration, displacement of local flora and fauna, and changes in trophic interactions, impacting ecosystem stability.
Rapid growth, abundant seed production, and allelopathic characteristics enhance its invasiveness, allowing it to outcompete indigenous species and modify ecosystem dynamics.

impact_findings.summary: In a tropical savanna, slight invasion (30% cover) did not change or lowered soil carbon and nitrogen fractions, and severe invasion (100% cover) significantly increased most of them. The authors conclude that the effect on soil carbon and nitrogen varies with invasion severity.
impact_findings.region_note: Plots with no, slight or severe invasion in a tropical savanna; the abstract does not name the site.
quotes: slight invasion did not alter or decreased the total and labile soil C and N fractions, and severe invasion significantly increased most of the total and labile soil C and N fractions
the impacts of invasion on soil C and N fractions could vary depending on invasion severity

impact_findings.affected: riparian vegetation, forest gaps and protected areas
impact_findings.summary: The authors describe the spread of Chromolaena odorata as alarming in two wildlife sanctuaries in Telangana, where it invades roadsides, forest gaps, protected areas and plantations, and where it is steadily destroying riparian vegetation along river banks.
impact_findings.region_note: Kinnerasani and Eturnagaram wildlife sanctuaries, Telangana, India.
quotes: The spread of devil weed is alarming in areas of podu cultivation, on the bunds of agricultural lands, wastelands, along roadsides, tracks, forest gaps, protected areas and plantations in the two said wildlife sanctuaries.
It is found invading new territories easily along the river banks and steadily destroying the riparian elements.

impact_findings.summary: In field experiments during oak woodland restoration, removing Microstegium vimineum benefited the growth and flowering of six native groundcover species planted in its patches. Planting several native species together gave no competitive suppression of the invader.
impact_findings.region_note: Oak woodland restoration plots, 2015 to 2016; the abstract does not name the site.
quotes: removal of Microstegium benefited the growth (and flowering) of native transplants in 2016, and all native species were more or less equally affected
there was no evidence of competitive suppression of Microstegium

impact_findings.summary: A two-year field experiment found that natural plant diversity did not resist invasion by Microstegium vimineum. The authors conclude that, at more productive sites, nearly complete removal of the invader is necessary to preserve plant species diversity.
impact_findings.region_note: A two-year field experiment in natural plant communities; the abstract does not name the site.
quotes: Diversity-mediated resistance did not effectively deter invasion by a highly competitive invader.
it would appear that nearly complete removal of this invader is necessary to preserve plant species diversity

impact_findings.summary: Winter mortality of the hemlock woolly adelgid was recorded at 100 sites from Maine to Georgia. Model projections under climate change showed increased winter survival and population growth over time, which the authors expect to raise its density across its current range, extend it northward and increase its impact on eastern hemlock.
impact_findings.region_note: Eastern North America; 100 sites from Maine to Georgia, 2014 to 2017, with model projections.
quotes: winter mortality of HWA was recorded at 100 sites from Maine to Georgia
Future projections under climate change showed increases in winter survival and population growth rates over time.

impact_findings.affected: eastern red-backed salamander in hemlock stands
impact_findings.summary: In southwestern Nova Scotia, infestation by the hemlock woolly adelgid reduced eastern red-backed salamander abundance, and imidacloprid treatment increased it.
impact_findings.region_note: Hemlock stands in southwestern Nova Scotia, Canada.
quotes: Treatment and infestation were the only predictors of abundance: treatment increased abundance, whereas infestation reduced it.

impact_findings.affected: plant diversity, crop yield, animals and people
impact_findings.summary: A review reports that Prosopis has invaded parts of wildlife reserves and national parks, that it can decrease the composition and diversity of plant species, and that it has adverse effects on crop yield and on animal and human health.
impact_findings.region_note: Ethiopia and similar arid and semi-arid areas. A literature review.
quotes: Prosopis has invaded parts of wildlife reserves and National Parks threatening biodiversity.
Prosopis has the capacity to decrease the composition and diversity of plant species and it has adverse effects on crop yield, as well as animal and human health.

impact_findings.affected: germination and growth of native plants
impact_findings.summary: A field survey found more new Prosopis recruits than recruits of native-associated plants, and aqueous leaf extract significantly reduced seed germination or seedling growth in the native Qatari plants tested.
impact_findings.region_note: A field site and laboratory extracts, Qatar.
quotes: Our field observations indicated a high prevalence of new recruitments of P. juliflora than other native-associated plants in the study site.
were significantly (p ≤ 0.05) reduced by the extracts at different concentration levels

impact_findings.summary: In Nairobi National Park, native plants that had grown alongside the invader grew shorter than naive natives. The results suggest that Parthenium hysterophorus may have selected for shorter native genotypes that show plasticity in competitive ability under drought.
impact_findings.region_note: Nairobi National Park, Kenya; seven native species compared as invader-experienced and naive individuals.
quotes: Invader-experienced natives grew shorter than naive natives regardless of growth conditions.
The results suggest that P. hysterophorus may have selected for shorter native plant genotypes that also exhibit plasticity in competitive ability under drought conditions.

impact_findings.summary: In mixed pine-oak forest in Mississippi, sites invaded by kudzu had lower species richness, less understory cover and a lower density of woody species than uninvaded sites.
impact_findings.region_note: Mixed pine-oak forest, Mississippi, USA; invaded and uninvaded sites compared.
quotes: Kudzu-invaded sites had lower species richness, less understory cover, and lower density of woody species than control sites.

impact_findings.summary: In experimental streams, brook trout living with brown trout moved less and were less evenly spread than brook trout living alone, which the authors read as interference competition by brown trout for access to foraging habitat outside thermal refuges.
impact_findings.region_note: Experimental streams; brook trout are native to eastern North America.
quotes: Allopatric brook trout showed greater movement rates and more even spatial distributions within streams than sympatric brook trout, suggesting interference competition by brown trout for access to forage habitats located outside thermal refugia.

impact_findings.summary: Laboratory trials found no evidence that Cuban treefrogs and native Florida treefrogs compete for refuges through behavioural or chemical cues. The native treefrogs could not avoid chemical cues from Cuban treefrogs even after living alongside them for 10 to 20 years, which the authors note matters for predation risk.
impact_findings.region_note: Laboratory trials with treefrogs native to Florida, USA.
quotes: We found no evidence of behavioral or chemical competition for refuges by Cuban treefrogs or native treefrogs.
The inability of native treefrogs to avoid chemical cues from Cuban treefrogs, despite living sympatrically with the invasive treefrogs for 10–20 years, has important implications for predation risk.
